statements.impact_statement: CVE-2025-15558 (GHSA-p436-gjf2-799p): on Windows, the Docker CLI plugin manager (github.com/docker/cli/cli-plugins/manager) searched C:\ProgramData\Docker\cli-plugins, a directory that a low-privileged user can create, so plugin binaries planted there could run with the privileges of the user invoking docker. The advisory states "This issue does not impact non-Windows binaries or projects that do not use the plugin manager code", lists github.com/docker/cli from 19.03.0 up to but not including 29.2.0 as affected, and links the fix, docker/cli pull request 6713 (commit 13759330b1f7), which removes that directory from the Windows-only plugin search list in cli-plugins/manager/manager_windows.go: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p436-gjf2-799p. The vulnerable code is not in this package. Read every published docker-cli-buildx package for Alpine 3.23 (0.33.0-r1 to 0.39.1-r1; 29 aarch64 and 28 x86_64 builds), each checked against the repository index checksum: each holds one program, /usr/libexec/docker/cli-plugins/docker-buildx, a Linux ELF executable (dynamically linked against musl through 0.39.0-r0, statically linked in 0.39.1-r0 and 0.39.1-r1) whose Go build information records GOOS=linux and github.com/docker/cli v29.3.1 to v29.9.3, all at or after the fixed 29.2.0. Go compiles manager_windows.go only into Windows binaries, so the Windows plugin search path is not in any of these programs. Listing the Go packages compiled into each program from its own function table confirms it: every build contains the docker/cli packages cli-plugins/plugin and cli-plugins/socket, no build contains the cli-plugins/manager package, and none contains the string ProgramData. The same listing does find cli-plugins/manager in /usr/bin/docker from the docker-cli 29.10.0-r1 package, which links it.

CVE-2025-15558 (GHSA-p436-gjf2-799p): on Windows, the Docker CLI plugin manager (github.com/docker/cli/cli-plugins/manager) searched C:\ProgramData\Docker\cli-plugins, a directory that a low-privileged user can create, so plugin binaries planted there could run with the privileges of the user invoking docker. Docker states that non-Windows binaries are not affected, and fixed it in docker/cli 29.2.0 by removing that directory from the Windows plugin search list: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p436-gjf2-799p, https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/6713, https://github.com/docker/cli/commit/13759330b1f7e7cb0d67047ea42c5482548ba7fa. This package contains no Go program and no Docker CLI code. We unpacked every published docker-dind-dev package for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine repository, 29.7.2-r0 to 29.10.0-r4 (60 builds, each for x86_64 and aarch64), after verifying each against its index checksum: the payload of each is the three shell scripts docker-entrypoint.sh, dockerd-entrypoint.sh and modprobe (29.7.2-r1 ships modprobe as /usr/lib/docker-dind/modprobe.sh), plus, from 29.9.2-r9, an SPDX document describing the programs of the separate packages it depends on. That document lists github.com/docker/cli 29.8.2, 29.9.3 or 29.10.0, all later than the 29.2.0 fix, but it is a JSON text file, not code. No build contains an ELF, PE or Mach-O file, a static archive or any other compiled program. github.com/docker/cli reaches an image only inside separately packaged programs, such as the docker command and docker-cli-buildx, which are assessed as their own owners; those are Linux builds as well.

CVE-2025-15558 (GHSA-p436-gjf2-799p, GO-2026-4610): Docker CLI for Windows searches C:\ProgramData\Docker\cli-plugins for plugin binaries, a directory a low-privileged user can create, so a Windows program that uses the plugin manager in the github.com/docker/cli/cli-plugins/manager package can run planted plugins. It is fixed in Docker CLI 29.2.0, which removes that path from the Windows plugin search list in cli-plugins/manager/manager_windows.go (https://github.com/docker/cli/security/advisories/GHSA-p436-gjf2-799p, https://github.com/docker/cli/commit/13759330b1f7e7cb0d67047ea42c5482548ba7fa, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4610); the advisory states that non-Windows binaries are not affected. We downloaded every published trivy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, 0.69.1-r0 to 0.74.0-r12 (38 builds) for both x86_64 and aarch64, and verified each against its index checksum. Each holds a single file, /usr/bin/trivy, a statically linked Go program built for Linux (GOOS=linux, CGO_ENABLED=0), so the Windows-only manager_windows.go is not compiled into it. Its build information lists github.com/docker/cli 29.2.1 to 29.7.2, but a byte search of every one of these 76 binaries, which covers the Go function and type names compiled into it, finds no name from github.com/docker/cli/cli-plugins/manager (including defaultSystemPluginDirs, the symbol the Go advisory lists) or from any other github.com/docker/cli/cli-plugins package: the plugin manager is not linked. The program does link other github.com/docker/cli packages, such as cli/config, which reads registry credentials. As a control, the same search finds runtime.main and cli/config functions in each of these binaries, and finds 115 matches for the cli-plugins/manager package in /usr/bin/docker from the DHI docker-cli 29.10.0-r1 package, which does link it, and in a Linux program we built for amd64 and arm64 against the vulnerable github.com/docker/cli 29.1.5 that imports the plugin manager, where it finds the package's names, defaultSystemPluginDirs among them. The Go symbol table of the newest build, 0.74.0-r12, likewise lists runtime.main and cli/config functions and no cli-plugins function.
